title: Detroit: the Chocolate Dandies jump band
summary: Joe was with Earle Warren at the Majestic Ballroom; Roy joined a non-reading jump band under Jimmy Tisdale and recalls how well the musicians dressed.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: He was with Earle Warren, working at the Majestic Ballroom. He had a good gig there. Very good gig. I got in with... He tried to get a couple of jobs down there, but I couldn't make it reading, you know. But I ended up with a little group that they called... They used to be the Nighthawks, then they changed their name to the Chocolate Dandies. This was below Hastings(?) Street. It was a (?)jump band(?).. They didn't read too well either, you know. Because we used to get a lot of music from Jean Goldkette, you know. Once we got past that introduction, if

we wasn't in that second ending, we was gonna end up in a big hassle, you know. So we'd get the tunes out and learn what we could of them, and put our little riffs on it, you know, and that was it, man.
That was a good little group, man. We sure did swing. I just got a picture of them somewhere where I'm sitting with a rifle. Have you ever see that picture?
Yeah, I'm about as big as this antenna here. I'm (?) somewhere, and I got a rifle. I don't know what happened to that rifle, you know...
Who was the leader in that band? Or was it like a cooperative?
No one was the leader, really. But Tisdale, Jimmy Tisdale was the director. He was from Pittsburgh.

The cats used to stay sharp, too, man. That's one thing back then. Those cats in those days really knew about dressing, you know. Now, the way they dress today, they used to do that on holidays(?)! Heh-heh. Really!
Now it's taken hold; that's the proper way to dress.
Yeah, and then I stayed around there for a while. That's when I first heard Bix.
No, he came in with ...(?)... one night.
